sentences.text: 6 04-10-2024 Heard Mr. Rajendra Narayan, the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioiner and Mr. Umeshanand Pandit, the learned APP for the State.
2. The petitioner seeks bail in connection with (Patna Sadar) Mahila P.S. Case No. 69 of 2016 dated 05.10.2016 instituted for the offences under Sections 376, 313, 415 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner was earlier twice rejected vide order dated 04.05.2018 in Cr. Misc. No. 61632 of 2017 and order dated 30.07.2021 passed in Cr. Misc. No. 3814 of Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.21522 of 2024(6) dt.04-10-2024 2021.
4.
However, the petitioner is now in custody since 24.11.2023 and there is no progress in the case before the Trial Court.
5. According to the accusation by Opposite Party No. 2, the petitioner came in contact with her and she started loving him.
She disclosed this fact to her husband also, after which her relationship with her husband turned sour.
She has further alleged that on the promise of marriage, the petitioner subjected her to sexual intercourse and also, at one point of time, forcibly got her aborted.

sentences.text: Mr. Rajendra Narayan, the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner has argued that though strictly speaking, a case under Section 376 of the IPC can be said to have been made out, but, if the accusations are analyzed a bit more deeper, it would appear that the relationship between the parties was consensual.

The O.P. No. 2 is a married lady, who Patna High Court CR. MISC.
No.21522 of 2024(6) dt.04-10-2024 continued with her liaison with the petitioner for a long time.

There is nothing in the entire investigation, which would indicate that the petitioner exerted such an influence over her that she did not know that the promise of marriage was only a sham and for the purpose of abstracting sexual favours from her.
There is no evidence of any abortion as well.
In this fact scenario, Mr. Narayan, has argued that it would at best be case of reneging on one's promise to marry.
Such backtracking of a person could be for myriad factors and not necessarily for cheating the victim.
7. The O.P. No. 2 was noticed earlier by this Court.
The notice appears to have been received by her mother.
An affidavit of jointness of O.P. No. 2 with her mother has also been filed by the petitioner.
8. This Court had called for a report from the Court below about the stage of the case.
The report indicates that nothing has happened and that not a single witness has been examined up till now.
Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.21522 of 2024(6) dt.04-10-2024 9.

Taking into account the afore-noted fact as also that the petitioner is in custody since 24.11.2023,
this Court is inclined to admit him to bail.

10. For the reasons aforesaid, the petitioner named above is directed to be released on bail on furnishing his bail bonds of Rs.10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned 1 st Class Judicial Magistrate, Patna in connection with (Patna Sadar) Mahila P.S. Case No. 69 of 2016.
